13. Why are the L and F suffixes used in Java?
Java requires suffixes for certain numeric literals:
literals because decimal literals are considered double by default.
Without these suffixes, Java treats the values as different data types and compilation may fail.
. What is Type Casting in Java?
Type Casting is the process of
converting data from one data type to another data type
When data stored in one type needs to be assigned to a variable of another type, Java converts the data into the destination type before storing it.
During this process, Java converts the internal representation of the data to match the destination data type. This conversion process is called
. Why is Type Casting required in Java?
Type Casting is required when the value of one data type needs to be stored in a variable of another data type.
A value stored in a byte variable may need to be stored in a short variable.
An int value may need to be stored in a double variable.
Since each data type has a different memory size and storage format, Java converts the data into the destination type before storing it.
